 Preview | UI students express excitement for the upcoming “Sunrise on the Reaping” movie adaptation
 The second prequel in “The Hunger Games” series, “Sunrise on the Reaping,” is set to premiere in theaters on Nov. 20. With Joseph Zada as Haymitch and Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner, the movie is predicted to be as successful as the original trilogy films. 
 Payton Terronez , Arts Reporter 
 • 
 November 16, 2026 
 Murray Close/Lionsgate Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. Photo Credit: Murray Close 
 On the morning of June 6, 2024, “Hunger Games” fans exulted like kids on Christmas Day at the announcement of “Sunrise on the Reaping” — the second prequel in the “Hunger Games” series — and the confirmed production of a movie adaptation. The movie adaptation releases in theaters Nov. 20. 
 From 2008 to 2010, Suzanne Collins published the original “Hunger Games” trilogy, which depicts a dystopian version of the U.S. where two children from 12 impoverished “districts” are reaped to fight to the death to entertain the upper-class “Capitol” as repercussions for losing a long-ago war. The protagonist is Katniss Everdeen, a 16-year-old girl from District 12 who volunteers to take her younger sister’s place in the 74th annual Hunger Games. 
 The trilogy received worldwide acclaim, winning 77 major literary awards combined. Lionsgate Entertainment later adapted the stories into films from 2012-15, with Collins as a producer. In 2020, over a decade after the final trilogy novel was completed, Collins released the first prequel, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” The prequel prompted a cultural resurgence of The Hunger Games Franchise, especially after the film adaptation released in 2023.  
 The second prequel, “Sunrise on the Reaping,” follows Haymitch Abernathy, victor of the 50th Hunger Games and Katniss Everdeen’s future mentor. Haymitch was reaped for the second Quarter Quell, which featured double the number of tributes.  
 University of Iowa first-year and longtime fan of the “Hunger Games” series, Reagan Zevenbergen , remembers buying “Sunrise on the Reaping” as soon as it hit the bookshelves. She appreciated how the prequel explored Haymitch as a character.  
 “I really liked getting to understand more about Haymitch’s backstory because it explains how he acts in the first book especially,” Zevenbergen said. “Collins did a really good job depicting heartbreaking events as well as giving minor characters from the first couple of books’ backstories.” 
 RELATED : UI students reflect on ‘Hunger Games’ franchise   
 After reading the book, UI first-year Claire Beeler is excited to see “Sunrise on the Reaping” come to life in theaters. Beeler has been keeping up with the film trailers and teased scenes.  
 “From the teasers, all the sets and visual effects look amazing, which makes the arena feel so real and immersive,” Beeler said. “The ‘Hunger Games’ movies are always action-packed, with a strong cast of actors who bring the book characters to life. This movie looks no different.” 
 The cast of “Sunrise on the Reaping” is made up of plenty of well-known stars, including Joseph Zada as young Haymitch, Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner, and Elle Fanning as young Effie Trinket. On the “Sunrise on the Reaping” press tour, Grace gained attention for her red carpet looks that paid homage to Jennifer Lawrence, who played Katniss in the original trilogy, and the costumes Katniss wore. Many fans fell in love with how Grace has put her own twists on the iconic and nostalgic outfits, including Zevenbergen.  
 “I’ve primarily seen Mckenna Grace’s looks on the red carpet, and I love them so much,” Zevenbergen said. “They’re all so beautiful and pay homage to Jennifer Lawrence. My favorite was Katniss’ wedding dress from ‘Catching Fire.’” 
 Longtime fans have grown to appreciate Collins’ inclusion of themes of socioeconomic inequality, authoritarian control, and propaganda throughout the series. Fans also enjoyed the surplus of dynamic characters in the series, the unique worldbuilding of the literary universe, and the dystopian setting. 
 UI first-year Reagan Easter has been a fan of “The Hunger Games” since she first read the trilogy in sixth grade. After enjoying “The Hunger Games” so much, she began to explore other dystopian series, but she knows nothing can compare to “The Hunger Games,” whether it’s the trilogy or the prequels.  
 “The Hunger Games never gets old,” Easter said. “I could reread the books and rewatch the movies for the rest of my life and notice a new detail every time.” 
 Upon hearing that “Sunrise on the Reaping” explored Haymitch’s backstory, Easter was excited to read and learn more about the mysterious District 12 mentor. Although the book elicited strong emotions, she considered such a strong reaction to be the true sign of an impactful story. 
 “I read ‘Sunrise on the Reaping,’ and I absolutely loved it. I remember thinking, ‘Suzanne Collins has truly done it again,’” Easter said. “I can’t wait to see the movie on Nov. 20.”
